guide.title: Colbert Hills: Golf in Manhattan, Kansas
guide.intro: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking places Colbert Hills eighth in Kansas, labelled "Public." The seven courses ranked above it — Prairie Dunes Country Club, Flint Hills National Golf Club, Shadow Glen Golf Club, Kansas City Country Club, Wolf Creek Kansas, Hallbrook Country Club and Milburn Country Club — are all labelled Private, which makes Colbert Hills the highest-ranked Public course on the list. It is a Kansas State University course in Manhattan, Riley County, designed by eight-time PGA Tour winner Jim Colbert along with architect Jeff Brauer. As of September 5, 2026, the course's own closures calendar shows the entire facility, course and restaurant together, closed all day September 13, 14 and 15, and again September 27, 28 and 29.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Colbert Hills is at 5200 Colbert Hills Drive, Manhattan, Kansas 66503, in Riley County. Manhattan Regional Airport (MHK) is 6.8 miles from the course by road. Kansas City International Airport (MCI), the larger hub, is 137.3 miles by road. From Topeka, the route runs 62.0 miles: I-70 west, then north on K-177 (Fort Riley Boulevard) into Manhattan, then Tuttle Creek Boulevard, Kimball Avenue, Vanesta Drive and Colbert Hills Drive.

sections.heading: The course
sections.body: The operator's own site states, "Designed by eight-time PGA Tour winner Jim Colbert along with architect Jeff Brauer." Wikipedia records that "the course opened with an invitational pro-am tournament on April 30, 2000," with an opening field of "Jim Colbert, Lee Trevino, Raymond Floyd, Annika Sörenstam and Manhattan native Deb Richard." Wikipedia also states Colbert Hills "was host to the Big 12 Conference women's golf championships on April 19–21, 2002." The course is home to the men's and women's golf teams of Kansas State University and is used by the university as an environmental research and turf management facility; it also houses the First Tee of Manhattan, including the Earl Woods National Youth Golf Academy. Wikipedia's infobox lists the course at par 72, 7,525 yards, rating 77.50; the operator's own homepage separately states the course spans 7,525 yards.

sections.heading: Rates and closures
sections.body: Colbert Hills publishes 2026 seasonal rates for April 1 through November 10: general public $115 Friday–Sunday and holidays, $105 Monday–Thursday, $80 twilight after 3 p.m. Monday–Thursday, with green fees and cart both included. Active Duty Military pays $95/$95/$80, Senior (60+) pays $90/$90/$80, and KSU Alumni Association members pay $90/$90/$80. The course's own rates page adds a qualifier that goes with every one of those figures: "All rates will change as we move through the season so check back with us. The Rates are adjusted for spring, summer, and fall and reflect the rack rate for golf or golf and cart." A ride-along fee applies at $25 per person (the operator's own page spells it "per peson"), and club rental runs $50 per set. Separately, the operator publishes a running closures calendar distinguishing "Entire Facility" closures from "Clubhouse"-only ones. Entire Facility closed all day: September 13, 14, 15, 27, 28 and 29, 2026; November 26; December 24 and 25. On November 25 the entire facility closes at 2 p.m. Clubhouse only, course unaffected: October 3, October 4, October 10, and September 25 from 5 p.m. The page gives no reason for any closure.

sections.heading: Basecamp: Manhattan
sections.body: On-site lodging is the Samy Family Stay & Play Lodge, which the operator describes as "an elegant lodge complex located directly behind the driving range at Colbert Hills" with "two sides, each featuring 4 sleeping rooms (8 total)." The course's own restaurant, Colbert's Bar & Grill, serves on site. In Manhattan, the Bluemont Hotel calls itself "The Premier Hotel of Manhattan, KS," and Tallgrass Tap House, also in Manhattan, titles its own site "Tallgrass Tap House | Manhattan, KS."

sections.heading: Day two: Wabaunsee Pines
sections.body: A second round is possible, but it is a separate trip: Wabaunsee Pines Golf Course, at Lake Wabaunsee in Alma, Kansas, sits 48.6 road miles from Colbert Hills. Its own site describes it as "a nine hole public golf course featuring limestone berms and native grasses of the Flint Hills." It is cash or check only and takes no tee times — its own site states, "We are a first come first served course." Its 2025 rates, effective January 1, 2025, were $15 for nine holes and $20 for eighteen, with cart rental at $15.

faq.question: How do I book a tee time at Colbert Hills?
faq.answer: Tee times are booked through the operator's own reservation system, linked from colberthills.com out to colberthills.cps.golf. That reservation subdomain blocks automated access entirely and has never been archived by the Wayback Machine, so exactly how many days in advance a tee time can be booked is not published anywhere this guide can verify — this guide says so plainly rather than guessing at a number. What is published: 2026 seasonal rates of $115 Friday–Sunday and holidays, $105 Monday–Thursday and $80 twilight, for April 1 through November 10, cart included, with the course's own note that rates change through the season. The entire facility is also closed on September 13, 14, 15, 27, 28 and 29, 2026, and again on November 26, December 24 and December 25; it closes at 2 p.m. on November 25.

faq.question: Is Colbert Hills closed anytime soon?
faq.answer: Yes. As of September 5, 2026, the course's own closures calendar shows the entire facility, course and restaurant together, closed all day September 13, 14 and 15, and again September 27, 28 and 29. The clubhouse alone, not the course, closes October 3, October 4 and October 10, and from 5 p.m. on September 25.

faq.question: What does a round cost?
faq.answer: From Colbert Hills' own 2026 seasonal rate table, April 1 through November 10: general public $115 Friday–Sunday and holidays, $105 Monday–Thursday, $80 twilight after 3 p.m. Monday–Thursday, green fees and cart included. The course's own page adds: "All rates will change as we move through the season so check back with us. The Rates are adjusted for spring, summer, and fall and reflect the rack rate for golf or golf and cart."

faq.question: Where is Colbert Hills?
faq.answer: 5200 Colbert Hills Drive, Manhattan, Kansas 66503, in Riley County. Manhattan Regional Airport (MHK) is 6.8 miles away by road, Kansas City International Airport (MCI) is 137.3 miles by road, and Topeka is 62.0 miles by road via I-70 west and K-177.

faq.question: Which courses were ranked above Colbert Hills?
faq.answer: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State list ranks seven courses above Colbert Hills — Prairie Dunes Country Club, Flint Hills National Golf Club, Shadow Glen Golf Club, Kansas City Country Club, Wolf Creek Kansas, Hallbrook Country Club and Milburn Country Club — but all seven carry the "Private" label. Colbert Hills, at #8, is the highest-ranked course labelled "Public."

faq.question: Is there a second course for a day two round?
faq.answer: Wabaunsee Pines Golf Course, at Lake Wabaunsee in Alma, Kansas, exists and is public — but it sits 48.6 road miles from Colbert Hills, so it is a separate trip rather than a same-day add-on. Its own site describes it as "a nine hole public golf course featuring limestone berms and native grasses of the Flint Hills," cash or check only, with no tee times taken.
